text:
lee: Heads-up: reproducible bug where SSE data lines are split inside UTF-8 multibyte sequences. Node/browser SDKs choke and trigger reconnect storms.

anya: Oof. Example?

lee: Server sends JSON {"id":7,"text":"café"} but bytes arrive as: chunk1 -> 'data: {"id":7,"text":"caf' chunk2 -> 'é"}

tom: That breaks naive newline-splitting parsers and JSON.parse throws

raj: Proxy layer? buffering?

lee: Seen with and without nginx in front. Also happens on poor mobile networks that split frames.

anya: Short fixes: client should decode with stream:true and keep partial text; server should try to flush whole SSE event at once.

tom: Agreed. Add these SDK options: sseKeepaliveMs default 10000, sseParseDebounceMs default 200. Also de-dupe by event id on reconnect.

raj: I tested nginx change (proxy_buffering off + proxy_request_buffering off) — much better but not perfect.

lee: Plan: 1) implement incremental parse in both SDKs; 2) add unit tests that feed artificial partial chunks; 3) docs with proxy/Envoy tips and sample headers (Cache-Control: no-transform, X-Accel-Buffering: no).

anya: Can we also emit comment keepalives from server (:keepalive

) so clients don't assume dead?

tom: Yes. I'll open the SDK PR for incremental parser + dedupe.

ci-bot: lee pushed sse/incremental-parser branch (CI: running)

lee: Thanks — once CI green, roll to staging and run Eva's chunked-write harness for 2h. Report back here. :thumbsup:
